finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the `f` query parameter is joined onto the root and read with no containment check, so an unauthenticated attacker can read arbitrary files readable by the process.
finding.source: files.go:12 `name := r.URL.Query().Get("f")` (attacker-controlled query string). Precondition: server reachable on :8082 (files.go:34 listens on all interfaces); no authentication on the route.
finding.sink: files.go:13 `os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name))`, response body written at files.go:18 `w.Write(data)`.

trace.note: /dl registered on default mux with no auth middleware
raw attacker string taken from `f` query parameter
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../../etc/passwd") calls Clean and resolves to "/etc/passwd"; file is opened and read
file contents written to HTTP response

finding.guards_checked: (1) No containment check comparing resolved path against root (fixed pattern from case 03 absent). (2) filepath.Join cleans `..` but does not confine the result. (3) No allowlist, extension check, or separator stripping on `name`. (4) No authentication or authorization on the route. (5) Error path only returns 404, which does not prevent reads of existing files. Absolute `name` values do not escape (Join concatenates under root) but `../` sequences do. Decoy case 26 does not apply: it canonicalises and checks containment, which this code does not do.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:32 registers /dl on the default mux with no auth middleware. files.go:12 takes the raw `f` value. files.go:13 joins it under root with no containment check, and filepath.Join cleans `../` so `../../../etc/passwd` resolves to /etc/passwd. files.go:14-16 only return 404 on error, and files.go:18 writes the file contents to the response. files.go:34 listens on all interfaces.
verdict.reason: An anonymous remote client can send `f=../../../etc/passwd` to /dl (files.go:12-13), and files.go:18 returns the contents of any file the process can read, with no auth or containment check anywhere on the path.
